newsitem.title: CHINA: China to clean up stock investment fund market.
newsitem.headline: China to clean up stock investment fund market.

text.p: China aims to clean up its stock investment fund market by stamping out rampant irregularities and training more specialised personnel, the Shanghai Securities News on Sunday quoted a senior official as saying.

At the end of October, China had 75 stock investment funds and 47 other kinds of funds, with total capital of 7.3 billion yuan, it quoted Zhou Daojiong, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, as telling a seminar in Beijing.
Despite the stated purpose of the funds, less than 10 percent of the money has been invested in stocks, making the establishment of such funds merely a means to raise money, Zhou said.
"The quality of managers of such funds is poor," Zhou said. "There have been many irregularities and some funds have been used to manipulate the market and do insider trading."
Zhou said most of the funds were set up when China lacked rules to govern the industry.
Beijing would shortly promulgate such rules and rectify the market, Zhou said. "Standardisation will be the key work for the fund market in the short term," he said.
This includes ensuring the funds focus their investment on securities, reinforcing risk control and fostering properly trained staff, he said.
Shanghai analysts said that Beijing in recent months has been studying how to support institutional investors in the stock market by allowing them to set up more stock investment funds.

Currently, such funds account for less than one percent of China's stock investment, with the stock market being dominated by retail investors who want quick profits instead of long-term investment, the analysts said.
